script:
Hello, this is The Portfolio Podcast for SOXX. Wednesday — here is your SOXX recap. The portfolio closed six point two two percent down on the session.

A semiconductor rout with no soft landing. Every single primary holding in this portfolio finished Wednesday's session in the red, with losses ranging from two point seven eight percent to ten point eighty percent. The Federal Reserve held rates steady for a fifth consecutive meeting, and the market answered harshly.

The broad market buckled under a combination of surging oil prices and the Federal Reserve's fifth consecutive rate hold. The S&P 500 fell one point five percent while the Nasdaq composite slumped one point seven percent, swinging sharply between gains and losses in the final hour of trading before closing decisively lower.

The biggest story of Wednesday's session belongs to KLA Corporation, which shed ten point eighty percent — the steepest decline across all ten primary holdings. That drop came against a backdrop of sector-wide pressure, but KLA's severity reflects its acute exposure to any softening in wafer fabrication equipment demand. Semiconductor equipment names have acted as leading indicators throughout this cycle, and when those stocks break sharply, the market is pricing in a deceleration further down the chip supply chain. Closely tied to that narrative, Applied Materials fell eight point forty percent, reinforcing the message. When two of the three major equipment suppliers move in tandem this aggressively, it is not noise — it is a signal about forward capital expenditure expectations across the foundry and memory segments. Watch for any guidance revisions from equipment customers in the weeks ahead.

Advanced Micro Devices was down five point five one percent on the session. That drop came despite the company finalizing a fifteen-year, fourteen billion dollar infrastructure partnership with Core Scientific, locking in more than five hundred megawatts of data center capacity. Analysts noted the deal underscores a meaningful shift — AI infrastructure is proving more lucrative than Bitcoin mining for Core Scientific — but the semiconductor selloff overwhelmed the headline entirely. The partnership is strategically significant; the timing of the announcement simply could not overcome broader macro pressure.

Micron Technology was down nine point nine four percent on the session. A major catalyst here was SK Hynix's fumbled earnings moment — the South Korean memory rival missed expectations, and that miss rippled directly through Micron as a proxy for global memory demand health. Separately, analysts covering agentic AI noted that memory demand could see a substantial next wave, but Wednesday's session was not the day the market rewarded that thesis.

NVIDIA was down three point five five percent on the session, making it the relative outperformer among the larger names. NVIDIA did announce a scheduled conference call for its second-quarter financial results, with a written chief financial officer commentary to be provided ahead of the call — a near-term catalyst worth tracking closely.

Broadcom was down two point seven eight percent on the session, the smallest decline in the portfolio Wednesday. A note circulating Wednesday pointed to the year-to-date performance of semiconductor leaders and raised valuation questions in the context of the Nasdaq correction, but Broadcom's relative resilience held.

Intel was down five point one two percent on the session. Intel has surged one hundred twenty-four percent year to date, and Wednesday's pullback reflects profit-taking pressure that has been building across the sector. Upcoming earnings will be the next true test.

Applied Materials was down eight point forty percent on the session. As noted in the top story, this move alongside KLA Corporation signals equipment spending anxiety across the chip supply chain.

KLA Corporation was down ten point eighty percent on the session — the hardest hit name in the portfolio Wednesday. No single company-specific catalyst emerged, making the severity of the move a pure expression of sector sentiment deterioration.

Marvell Technology was down six point three four percent on the session. Marvell sits at the intersection of custom silicon and data center networking, and names in that space bore the brunt of Wednesday's AI-driven rout without the buffer of a major headline to anchor investor attention.

Lam Research was down six point four zero percent on the session. Like Applied Materials and KLA Corporation, Lam Research operates in the semiconductor equipment segment, and Wednesday's session confirmed that the entire equipment tier moved together. Watch capital expenditure commentary from major foundry customers as the primary signal for this group.

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing was down four point five zero percent on the session. As the world's leading contract chipmaker, its move tracked the broader sector decline. Any shift in foundry utilization guidance will be a key variable for this holding.

Three numbers to watch in the next forty-eight hours. First, NVIDIA's second-quarter earnings call — the written chief financial officer commentary drops ahead of the call and will set the tone for AI infrastructure spending expectations across the entire portfolio. Second, any Federal Reserve speaker commentary following Wednesday's rate hold decision, which could clarify the path forward on rates and ease or deepen the pressure on growth-oriented technology names. Third, monitor SK Hynix's full earnings release details, as the specifics of their miss will directly inform the memory demand picture for Micron Technology heading into its own reporting cycle.

This is The Portfolio Podcast for SOXX. We will be back same time the next business day with tomorrow's news. Watch NVIDIA's pre-call commentary closely — it may be the single most important data point this portfolio sees in the next forty-eight hours.
